data.description:
# Context
GitHub code scanning (CodeQL) reports 5 open findings, all rule `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data` ("Clear-text logging of sensitive information"), operator-directed into the bug bash 2026-08-12:

- alert 83 — src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:199
- alert 84 — src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:204
- alert 85 — src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:221
- alert 86 — src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:452
- alert 87 — src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:512

Line numbers are as of the scan's most recent instance — re-locate the flagged expressions on CURRENT origin/main before fixing. For each site, determine whether the logged value is genuinely sensitive (a secret/token/credential/signing key reaching a log or stdout in clear text) or a CodeQL false positive (e.g. a value CodeQL taints as "secret" that is actually a non-secret identifier). Fix real ones by redacting/omitting the value (log its presence, length, or fingerprint — never the value); dismiss false positives via the code-scanning API with a documented reason ONLY if genuinely false, and record the justification on this ticket.

# Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1 — Each of the 5 flagged expressions is either fixed (no sensitive value reaches any log/stdout in clear text) or dismissed with a recorded, evidence-backed false-positive justification on this ticket.
- [ ] AC2 — Tests pin the fixed sites: the sensitive value does not appear in captured log output for the exercised paths (caplog-based, deterministic).
- [ ] AC3 — After the fix lands, the code-scanning alert count for this rule is 0 open (or only documented dismissals) — evidence via `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/code-scanning/alerts` output or [operator-attested].
- [ ] AC4 — `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; no behavior change beyond log content.
data.title: CodeQL: 5 clear-text logging of sensitive information findings
